Landlord associations told the board the cap would discourage maintenance spending, arguing that owners facing capped revenue would defer roof and boiler replacement until failure. Enforcement will run through the existing housing office, which supervisors were told would need two additional staff to handle complaints. The board also directed staff to report back after eighteen months with data on vacancy rates, average increases and the number of exemption claims filed, a review that supporters framed as the condition for keeping the measure and opponents described as too distant to matter. Two supervisors who voted against said they would introduce a separate measure offering tax relief for owners who complete energy upgrades, arguing that incentives work better than caps. The chair closed the hearing by noting that more than sixty residents had signed up to speak and that the board had sat for over five hours. Reviews published at launch were broadly positive about the setting and mixed on pacing, with several noting that the middle section asks players to repeat travel across the same terrain more often than the design supports. The studio said a patch addressing save issues was already in preparation and would arrive within two weeks, following reports from players whose progress failed to persist after quitting during certain sequences. The reworked opening replaces what the director described as an extended tutorial with a shorter sequence that introduces mechanics through the first major location instead. Performance on previous-generation consoles was the stated reason for the second delay, and early testing suggests the target frame rate holds outside the largest settlement, where drops remain noticeable. The studio employs about ninety people and has said publicly that it did not extend working hours during the delay period, a claim two staff members repeated in interviews this week. Sales figures were not released, though the game reached the upper positions of two digital storefronts on the first day. A story expansion is planned but has no date, and the director said the team would take a break before beginning work on it. Retailers reported that physical editions sold through more slowly than the digital version, a pattern the studio said reflected its decision not to fund a large boxed print run. The publisher confirmed that no additional content had been cut during either delay and that the shipped game matches the feature list published two years ago. Community managers said they would post a schedule for the first three patches within days.

article_a_text: The studio behind Ashfall Country has pushed the game's release back by four months, citing performance work on older consoles. Pre-orders will be honoured at the original price. It is the second delay for the title.

article_b_text: Following Thursday's announcement of a four-month delay, the developers of Ashfall Country told players that no planned areas or features had been removed and that the additional time is going into frame-rate work on previous-generation machines. The studio said staff would not be asked to work extended hours. Pre-order pricing stands.

article_a_text: The musical Ferryman's Daughter opened at a West End theatre on Thursday after a run in the north, with a cast of twenty-two and a score performed by a twelve-piece band. Producers said the transfer had been planned since the spring. Booking runs to March.

article_a_text: A rival streaming platform has cancelled the drama Northgate after two seasons, telling the production team the decision reflects viewing figures against cost. The final episodes remain available. Producers said they would look for another home for a planned third run.

article_a_title: Salt Harbour Takes Top Prize at Vireo Festival
article_a_text: The drama Salt Harbour won the main award at the Vireo Film Festival on Saturday, with the jury praising its handling of a small fishing town's decline. It is the first feature by its director to compete at the festival, having been developed through a regional funding scheme over four years. Distribution deals for three territories were signed during the week, and the producers said talks continue for two more. The jury president described the decision as reached without extended argument. A second prize went to a documentary about seasonal labour.
article_b_title: The Quiet Ledger Wins Aldermoor Prize
article_b_text: The novel The Quiet Ledger won the Aldermoor Prize for fiction on Tuesday evening, with the chair of judges describing the book's structure as its central achievement. The author becomes the second debut writer to take the award in a decade, and the first to do so with a book published by a house of fewer than ten staff. The prize carries 50,000, and past winners have typically seen sales increase several times over in the months that follow. Judges said the decision came after three rounds of discussion, with two other titles remaining in contention until the final session. The chair noted that the shortlist had been unusually varied in form. The winner said she had written most of the book in the year after leaving a job in shipping insurance.
